Package frc.DELib25.Subsystems.Swerve.SwerveUtil

Class SwerveConstants

java.lang.Object
frc.DELib25.Subsystems.Swerve.SwerveUtil.SwerveConstants
public abstract class SwerveConstants extends Object
Central configuration for a swerve drivetrain.

This class holds:

  • Identity & CAN bus configuration
  • Module device IDs and CANcoder offsets
  • Robot mass and geometry (for kinematics & simulation)
  • Motion limits and drive-to-point constraints
  • SysId characterization configs
  • Drive/steer PID and choreo/auto controllers
  • Module & drivetrain constants for CTRE Phoenix 6 swerve

Most physical quantities use the WPILib units API (e.g. Distance, LinearVelocity, Angle, Current) so the underlying units can be changed centrally without renaming fields.

    • WHEEL_COEFFICIENT_OF_FRICTION

      public edu.wpi.first.units.measure.Dimensionless WHEEL_COEFFICIENT_OF_FRICTION
      Coefficient of friction of the wheels on the carpet.

      How to find:

      1. Weigh the robot to find the normal force (N).
      2. Push the robot with a spring scale until it starts to move, record that force (F).
      3. Compute μ = F / N and use that value here.

    • SKEW_COMPENSATION_SCALAR

      public edu.wpi.first.units.measure.Dimensionless SKEW_COMPENSATION_SCALAR
      Scalar to compensate for skew when driving straight (e.g. imperfect center of rotation, uneven weight distribution).

      Should be near 1.0. Values > 1.0 or < 1.0 can bias the drive outputs to keep the robot straight under load.

    • getDefaultSwerveModuleConstants

      protected com.ctre.phoenix6.swerve.SwerveModuleConstants<com.ctre.phoenix6.configs.TalonFXConfiguration,com.ctre.phoenix6.configs.TalonFXConfiguration,com.ctre.phoenix6.configs.CANcoderConfiguration> getDefaultSwerveModuleConstants()
      Constructs a base set of SwerveModuleConstants using:
      • Default drive/steer configs from getDefaultDriveTalonFXConfig() and getDefaultSteerTalonFXConfig()
      • Gear ratios and inversion from MODULE_HARDWARE_CONSTANTS
      • Slot0 drive and steer gains from DRIVE_SLOT0_CONFIGS and STEER_SLOT0_CONFIGS

      Additional per-module IDs, offsets, and locations are applied in getDefaultSwerveModuleConstantsArray().
